def_original: Stakeholder capacity to influence the firm via coercive utilitarian or normative means (Mitchell et al. 1997).
def_operational: In the named incident a person or group could force withhold delay override or stop a recovery action.
not_this: Did you experience a power problem; Power as a theme title

def_original: Generalized perception that a claim or claimant is proper or appropriate within a socially constructed system of norms (Mitchell et al. 1997).
def_operational: In the named incident a claim to a service or restore order was treated as rightful or as out of line.
spoken_standin: right to ask; out of line; outside their role
not_this: Did you experience a legitimacy problem; NIST scoring; Legitimacy as a theme title

def_original: Degree to which a stakeholder claim calls for immediate attention combining time sensitivity and criticality (Mitchell et al. 1997).
def_operational: In the named incident a time-critical demand reordered attention or a claimed clock was not acted on.
not_this: Spoken codebook word urgency unless the participant said it first; Urgency as a theme title

def_original: Mitchell et al. 1997 two-attribute type: power plus legitimacy.
def_operational: Leverage memo only: both power and legitimacy examples (or documented boundaries) exist in the named incident.
not_this: Delve theme title Dominant; forced choice power or legitimacy

def_original: Mitchell et al. 1997 two-attribute type: power plus urgency.
def_operational: Leverage memo only: both power and urgency examples exist in the named incident.

def_original: Mitchell et al. 1997 two-attribute type: legitimacy plus urgency.
def_operational: Leverage memo only: both legitimacy and urgency examples exist in the named incident.

def_original: Mitchell et al. 1997 three-attribute type: power legitimacy and urgency.
def_operational: Leverage memo only: all three attributes have a concrete example or documented boundary in the named incident.
spoken_standin: not spoken; memo after L and A-C
not_this: Delve theme title Definitive; a finding that confirms Mitchell types

def_original: No original Mitchell type. This study name for the enacted combination of P L and/or U.
def_operational: Who actually moved restore order delayed an action or redefined done plus what supplied that pull in one named ITDRPaaS event.
spoken_standin: who moved / who could have stopped it; position written rule clock something else; pull
not_this: A fourth salience attribute; spoken word leverage; unclear recoded as a type

def_original: Not a Mitchell attribute. PQ2 enactment of who was authorized to decide.
def_operational: Who was supposed to make the call on the restoration tradeoff versus who actually made it including authority needed but absent.
spoken_standin: who was supposed to make the call and who actually made it
not_this: Org-chart finding detached from the incident; theme titled Decision Rights

def_original: Not a Mitchell attribute. PQ2 enactment of how a stalled or contested claim was moved upward or outward.
def_operational: What triggered an escalation and whether it sped slowed or changed done. Nothing escalated is boundary no_escalation.
spoken_standin: what if anything triggered an escalation; did it speed slow or change done
not_this: Failed interview if nothing was escalated; theme titled Escalation

def_original: Not a Mitchell attribute. PQ2 enactment of what counted as enough proof of recovery.
def_operational: What the manager treated as enough proof and whether anyone asked for different proof mid-incident.
not_this: NIST ISO BCM scoring; theme titled Evidence

def_original: Reviewable decision-relevant evidence that prioritized services can be restored within tolerance (project-plan assurance sources; verify).
def_operational: What the manager would point to (log test approval ticket or verbal reconstruction) to defend restoration. Path C is no_reviewable_proof.
spoken_standin: what would you point to if you had to defend that restoration
not_this: Audit of the artifact; Path C as invalid data

def_original: Patterned accounts of events decisions and conditions; theoretically informed items permitted (Caelli et al. 2003; Kahlke 2014; Percy et al. 2015).
def_operational: Managers accounts of one named ITDRPaaS incident and the objects used in it.

def_original: Focused account of a named incident (Flanagan 1954; Chell 2004; Butterfield et al. 2005).
def_operational: Q0 opening: one disruption failover test or operational recovery in 36 months.
spoken_standin: Please walk me through one specific disruption failover recovery test or operational recovery
not_this: Guest et al. 2006 as the interview method

def_original: Deductive template plus inductive codes (Fereday and Muir-Cochrane 2006).
